headline: GOLD SLIDES TO $3,537 AS SILVER POSTS WORST WEEK OF 2026 — Dollar Near 19-Month High, Dec Fed Hike Odds Hit 97%
snippet: Spot gold fell to $3,537 on Sunday, down roughly 3% on the week, as a surging US dollar held near a 19-month high and markets priced in a 97% chance of a December Federal Reserve rate hike. Silver suffered even sharper losses, tracking toward a 13% weekly decline — its worst drop of 2026. Gold remains 34.5% below its January 29 all-time closing high of $5,405.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SURGES 11% BACK FROM POST-EARNINGS SELLOFF — MP Materials Gains 4% As Traders Eye US-China Talks
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) rebounded 11% as beaten-down rare earth names stabilized after a bruising week. MP Materials climbed 4% and United States Antimony edged higher as investors positioned ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting. USAR had been hammered after Q3 earnings missed expectations, compounded by a William Blair downgrade citing feedstock shortages at its Less Common Metals unit.

headline: COPPER STEADIES ABOVE $14,000 AFTER 2.5-MONTH LOW — Chinese Buyers Pay Record $360/Ton Import Premium Amid Futures Chaos
snippet: LME copper found tentative support above $14,000 per tonne after last week's 5.7% single-day collapse — its worst in 19 months — as the AI trade unwound across London, New York, and Shanghai. Meanwhile, Chinese smelters were paying a record $360/ton import premium for physical copper, suggesting the selloff was driven by futures liquidation rather than collapsing end-user demand.

headline: CRITICAL METALS (CRML) DOWN 28.7% ON THE WEEK — Greenland Acquisition Dilution Sends Stock 84% Below 52-Week High
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (Nasdaq: CRML) fell 28.7% week-to-date through November 19, driven by an updated development roadmap and significant share dilution tied to its Greenland rare earth acquisition. The stock is now 84.1% below its 52-week high, a sharp reversal for one of the most-watched rare earth names of 2025-2026.

headline: URANIUM MINERS DOWN 31% YEAR-TO-DATE WHILE SPOT HOLDS AT $90/LB — TradeTech Long-Term Price Sets Nominal Record at $99
snippet: The Sprott Uranium Miners ETF (URNM) fell to its lowest close since May 2025, now down 31% year-to-date, while spot uranium sits at $90.02/lb — up 10% for the year. TradeTech's long-term uranium price simultaneously hit a nominal record of $99/lb. Analysts debate whether the equity-to-commodity disconnect reflects financing risk, operator execution concerns, or a classic junior mining overcorrection.

headline: NRC GRANTS NEW MEXICO DOJ INTERVENTION IN CROWNPOINT URANIUM MINE RESTART — Public Hearing Ordered Before Licensing Resumes
snippet: A panel of the NRC's Atomic Safety and Licensing Board granted the New Mexico DOJ's petition to intervene in the licensing renewal for the Crownpoint Uranium Project, home to the Church Rock and Crownpoint in-situ recovery sites. The ruling orders a formal public hearing before any restart can proceed, adding a regulatory obstacle to what had been one of the more advanced US uranium project pipelines.

headline: BLUE MOON METALS CLOSES TURNER COPPER-GOLD ACQUISITION IN OREGON — Enters US Development Pipeline With Drill-Ready Asset
snippet: Blue Moon Metals has completed its acquisition of the Turner copper-gold deposit in Oregon, US. The deal advances the company's US-focused development strategy and positions it for resource expansion drilling at Turner in 2027. The closure on November 20 follows weeks of regulatory and financing preparations.

headline: SCORPION MINERALS SIGNS BINDING DEAL FOR 289 SQ KM PAYNES FIND GOLD PROJECT — Milestone-Linked Payments Cap Upfront Risk
snippet: ASX-listed Scorpion Minerals (SCN) has executed a binding agreement to acquire the Paynes Find gold project in Western Australia, covering 289 square kilometres of prospective ground. The deal structure ties payments to future resource definition milestones, limiting upfront capital outlay while securing access to a large, underexplored ground package in a proven gold district.

headline: UR-ENERGY ADVANCES LOST SOLDIER URANIUM PROJECT WITH BASELINE FIELD STUDIES — Wyoming ISR Asset Takes Next Development Step
snippet: Ur-Energy has launched a series of baseline environmental and technical studies at its Lost Soldier uranium project in Wyoming, the standard first step toward advancing an in-situ recovery operation toward production. The company has not yet issued formal production guidance, but the fieldwork initiation signals active permitting intent as US uranium demand projections rise.

headline: IVANHOE SLASHES KAMOA-KAKULA 2027 COPPER OUTPUT FORECAST 19% — DRC Flood Recovery Slower Than Expected, Open-Pit Bridge Planned
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines cut its 2027 Kamoa-Kakula copper production target by 19% in its Q3 update, citing slower-than-expected recovery from flooding in the DRC. Full-year 2026 output is guided at approximately 290,000 tonnes. To bridge the gap, the company plans to begin surface waste stripping in Q1 2027, with first open-pit ore targeted for Q3 2027. Cash costs for 2027 were raised to $2.50-$3.00/lb.

headline: COPPER SELLOFF: FORCED LIQUIDATION OR REAL DEMAND CRACK? Analysts Split After AI Trade Unwind Hits $14,000
snippet: Copper's 5.7% single-day plunge on November 18 — driven by the unwinding of AI-linked metals positions — left analysts divided. The bearish case: weakening tech capex forecasts genuinely reduce copper demand. The bull case: Chinese smelters paying a record $360/ton import premium while futures sold off suggests strong physical demand is being obscured by financial-market noise.

headline: WHEATON PRECIOUS METALS: THE LOWER-RISK WAY TO OWN THE GOLD CORRECTION — Why Streamers Outperform Miners in Drawdowns
snippet: With gold miners like Barrick trading near 52-week lows ($31.93 vs. a $54.69 high) and Coeur near $13 versus a $27.77 peak, analysts are revisiting royalty and streaming names. Wheaton Precious Metals is highlighted as offering gold exposure while insulating investors from cost inflation that squeezes producers — a structural advantage in the current environment of high energy and labour costs.
